purpose: Fail-closed manufacture/install interface contract for the benchmark-close municipal slide. The prior generated slide had a roughly 2 m platform and chute but no climbable stair/access assembly and no explicit head/runout support path. This contract adds period-plausible stair geometry, support interfaces and LOD requirements without awarding Visual Fidelity points from source evidence.

referenceBasis.topic: standard drawing for large playground slide SU-L
requirementsUsed: large slide includes an explicit stair/access section (階段) and platform
stair tread depth 170 mm or greater
sliding surface stainless plate 1.5 mm or greater
large-slide major steelwork is a separately supported fabricated assembly with dedicated ascent and landing foundations
referenceBasis.historicalContext: The Yokohama standard-drawing lineage listed in the same document includes partial revisions in April 1999 and April 2002. The 2018 sheet is therefore used as a construction-principle and safety-envelope reference, not as proof that every detail matches one exact circa-2000 manufacturer product.

referenceBasis.topic: fictional scene slide envelope and material classes
requirementsUsed: 2.0 mm modeled SUS304 sliding skin and side sheets
four LOD levels with animated cross-fade
generated visual shell adds no gameplay collider

assemblySequence: below-grade/foundation interface retained by existing gameplay ground
two coated-steel access handrails and platform transition rails
existing coated-steel platform and support frame
coated-steel chute-head bearing crossmember tied back to the platform frame
existing continuous 2 mm SUS304 chute shell and raised side sheets
coated-steel runout bearing crossmember with two short support posts and foot plates
LOD0-only exposed fastener heads at the chute-head bearing interface
manufactureReconstruction.mounting: The access stair climbs from grade on local -Z to the rear edge of the existing platform. Horizontal treads seat on both inclined stringers. Stringers terminate into foot plates at grade and continue to the platform underside. Access handrails follow the stair pitch and bridge into the existing platform guard posts. The chute head bears on a transverse frame member linked to the existing support legs; the low runout bears on a transverse member with two short ground-supported posts.
manufactureReconstruction.interfacesAndSeals: No decorative sealant or painted contact shadow is permitted. Steel-to-steel joints may use millimetric intentional overlap consistent with welded/bolted fabrication. Positive daylight gaps between tread and stringer, stringer and foot plate, chute and either bearing member, or top tread and platform access are source-side failures.
manufactureReconstruction.orientation: Local +Z is the descending chute direction. Access stairs rise toward local +Z from the rear at local -Z. Treads remain horizontal; stringers and handrails follow approximately 50.9 degrees above horizontal.
manufactureReconstruction.exposure: Tread tops, handrails and platform receive strong midsummer UV/rain and hand/foot contact. Stringer undersides and chute-head hardware are partially sheltered. Ground plates and runout supports receive splash and persistent near-grade contamination.
manufactureReconstruction.aging: Paint chalking follows UV exposure; handrails receive local polish; tread noses receive directional foot abrasion; near-grade plates receive splash darkening and restrained ferrous oxidation at real steel sources only. SUS304 travel abrasion follows the chute direction and is not represented as random rust.
manufactureReconstruction.geometryVsMaterialDetail: Tread count/depth/thickness, stringers, rails, foot plates, bearing crossmembers, posts and visible fastener heads are geometry. Checker-plate relief below silhouette scale, paint orange-peel/chalking, fine abrasion, local polish, micro-rust and water residue are material/weathering detail.
manufactureReconstruction.lodPolicy: LOD0/1/2/3 all retain the ten-step stair silhouette, stringers, access rails, head bearing and runout support to prevent topology-scale popping. Only LOD0 retains small chute-head fastener heads. All new renderers must be rebound into the corresponding existing HD_Slide LOD renderer set with animated cross-fade.

coatedStructuralSteel.microstructure: subtle baked/powder-coat orange peel and age-related chalking; checker tread relief remains material-scale where below silhouette resolution
coatedStructuralSteel.uvAging: upward and sun-facing surfaces chalk/desaturate more strongly than sheltered undersides
coatedStructuralSteel.angularResponse: dielectric Fresnel from real sun/sky/probes; no painted highlight

exposedFastenerSteel.microstructure: fine galvanizing/machining and restrained oxidation variance
exposedFastenerSteel.angularResponse: metallic reflection from the actual environment

stainlessChute.microstructure: fine directional travel abrasion without painted specular streaks
stainlessChute.wetness: lower apparent roughness only when an explicit rain/wet state is active
stainlessChute.uvAging: no paint chalking; contamination and fine abrasion only
stainlessChute.angularResponse: strong grazing reflection driven by BRDF/Fresnel and real environment

stringer floating above its grade foot plate
top tread separated from platform by an unstepable gap
new access renderer left outside HD_Slide LODGroup
